newsitem.title: ITALY: AgipPetroli, Kuwait deal becomes operative.
newsitem.headline: AgipPetroli, Kuwait deal becomes operative.

text.p: Kuwait's deal with AgipPetroli, the refining and marketing arm of Italian energy group ENI, for a 50 percent share in the firm's Milazzo refinery, became operative on Monday, ENI said in a statement.

In the deal worth around one trillion lire ($650 million), AgipPetroli transferred the 50 percent stake to Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC)'s Kuwait Petroleum Italia unit, as well as 336 filling stations in Italy.
The deal, for which a letter of intent was signed in October, had been subject to approval by Italy's Antitrust authority which was given on December 19.

The accord also provides for the upgrading of the Sicilian refinery to produce higher quality products and become more competitive. Milazzo has a current annual capacity equal to some eight million tonnes.
The 336 Italian filling stations have an annual throughput of about 500 million litres (110 million imperial gallons), or 1.5 percent of the Italian retail market.
KPC said in October the deal allowed it to re-enter the Italian oil refinery industry and would expand its retail activity in Italy. KPC closed its refinery in Naples in 1993.
ENI said the accord also allowed AgipPetroli to optimise its own position in the refining, logistics and distribution sectors.
